title: Microsoft Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 enter their ‘permanently vulnerable’ era
content_md: Note: Create your free account in SOCFortress Signals ( https://signals.socfortress.co/ ) for: Global intelligence Security advisories, search & filters Microsoft Patch Tuesday & CISA KEV views Threat actor, malware & IOC views Source references, visualizations & timeline Intro Microsoft has officially declared that Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 are now permanently vulnerable because official support and vulnerability testing have completely concluded. Although standard support ended in October 2025, a short-term paid extension was granted to accommodate reluctant users before expiring entirely in October 2026. The tech giant has strongly urged organizations still utilizing these legacy platforms to upgrade immediately to newer systems or online alternatives. Meanwhile, current security patches are exclusively being directed toward the Subscription Edition to address critical flaws like remote code execution. Ultimately, companies failing to migrate their infrastructure will face unmitigated security risks with zero ongoing protection from the vendor Strategic Timeline of Legacy Support Lifecycle The retirement of legacy Microsoft Exchange platforms followed a multi-stage lifecycle, progressing through initial support terminations, temporary extensions, and the final cessation of security maintenance: October 14, 2025 : Official End of Support reached for both Exchange Server 2016 and Exchange Server 2019. July 2025 : Vendor announcement of the Extended Security Updates (ESU)
exclude_reason: SOCFortress Medium piece opens with a product-signup pitch and is a generic explainer of the Exchange 2016/2019 support expiration already covered by the existing 'Security Updates End in October' story. No new event substance.
